title: 2009 HMMT November Guts Problem 17
statement: A circle passes through the points \((2,0)\) and \((4,0)\) and is tangent to the line \(y=x\). Find the sum of all possible values for the \(y\)-coordinate of the center of the circle.

solutions.text: -6 First, we see that the x coordinate must be 3. Let the y coordinate be y. Now, we see that the radius is \(r=\sqrt{1+y^{2}}\). The line from the center of the circle to the point of tangency with the line \(x=y\) is perpendicular to the line \(x=y\). Hence, the distance from the center of the circle to the line \(x=y\) is \(d=\sqrt{2}(3-y)\). Letting \(r=d\) we see that the two possible values for y are 1 and -7 , which sum to -6 .
